title: Collars, cuffs and waistbands that sit crisp and flat

say: Collars, cuffs and waistbands that sit crisp and flat.
This is the video for module two of Fashion Finishing and Quality Control.
Collars, cuffs and waistbands sit close to the face, hands and waist, so clients notice every bump.

panel.heading: Clients notice every bump here
items: Collars sit close to the face
Cuffs are always judged as a pair

say: The crisp finish comes from four skills: interfacing, trimming and grading seams, understitching, and careful matching.

panel.heading: Clients notice every bump here
items: Collars sit close to the face
Cuffs are always judged as a pair

say: Choose interfacing a little lighter than the fabric, and test-fuse a scrap first. Press, do not slide, often 10 to 15 seconds in each position. Keep the iron on its heel between presses, and let the collar cool flat.

panel.heading: A Peter Pan collar that rolls under
items: Fuse interfacing to the upper collar
Trim the under collar 2 to 3 mm smaller

say: Fabric loses a little length on the outside of a fold. So trim 2 to 3 mm off the outer edge of the under collar. The upper collar bubbles slightly, and that extra lets the seam roll underneath, where nobody sees it.

panel.heading: A Peter Pan collar that rolls under
items: Fuse interfacing to the upper collar
Trim the under collar 2 to 3 mm smaller
panel.rule: Trim the under collar 2 to 3 mm smaller, so the seam rolls under.

say: After sewing, grade the seam: under collar allowance to about 3 mm, upper to about 6 mm. Notch the curves. Then understitch the allowances to the under collar, turn, roll and press.
Sew every collar on a card template, so both ends match.

panel.heading: A Peter Pan collar that rolls under
items: Fuse interfacing to the upper collar
Trim the under collar 2 to 3 mm smaller
panel.rule: Trim the under collar 2 to 3 mm smaller, so the seam rolls under.

say: Stand collars must stand up evenly. Staystitch the neckline as soon as it is cut. A stretched neckline is the most common reason a stand wrinkles at the back.

cards.d: A curved neckline stretches easily. Staystitch it as soon as it is cut, and handle it flat.
A stand must hold itself upright, so it needs firmer interfacing than a flat collar.
Take one or two stitches across a collar point, trim, then turn with a point turner.

say: A stand needs firmer interfacing than a flat collar, because it must hold itself upright.

cards.d: A curved neckline stretches easily. Staystitch it as soon as it is cut, and handle it flat.
A stand must hold itself upright, so it needs firmer interfacing than a flat collar.
Take one or two stitches across a collar point, trim, then turn with a point turner.

say: For sharp shirt collar points, take one or two stitches across the point instead of pivoting. Trim, then push the point out with a point turner, never with sharp scissors.

cards.d: A curved neckline stretches easily. Staystitch it as soon as it is cut, and handle it flat.
A stand must hold itself upright, so it needs firmer interfacing than a flat collar.
Take one or two stitches across a collar point, trim, then turn with a point turner.

say: For example, Funmi in Port Harcourt is sewing a senator top. The stand is 42 cm between the centre front marks. But the sewn neckline measures 43.2 cm.

panel.heading: Funmi measures before she sews
items: Ease it back to 42 cm, mostly at the back
Steam flat, then attach the stand

say: It is 1.2 cm too long, so it stretched in handling. She runs a line of long stitches inside the seam allowance and pulls it up to 42 cm, mostly over the back and shoulders. Then she attaches the stand, with no ripples.

panel.heading: Funmi measures before she sews
items: Ease it back to 42 cm, mostly at the back
Steam flat, then attach the stand
panel.rule: Measure the neckline and the stand before you attach.

say: For example, Esther in Jos has a client with a 16 cm wrist. She adds 4 cm ease and a 2 cm overlap, for a finished cuff of 22 cm.

panel.heading: Esther calculates a cuff
panel.rule: Cuff = wrist + ease + overlap + two seam allowances.

say: With 1 cm seam allowances, she cuts it 24 cm long. The cuff folds in half, so for a 6 cm cuff she cuts 14 cm high.

panel.heading: Esther calculates a cuff
panel.rule: Cuff = wrist + ease + overlap + two seam allowances.

say: The sleeve hem is 32 cm, but the cuff closes over 20 cm, so she gathers in 12 cm. She puts most of the fullness towards the back, where the elbow bends.

panel.heading: Esther calculates a cuff
panel.rule: Cuff = wrist + ease + overlap + two seam allowances.

say: Lay the two cuffs side by side. Check the same width, the same height, and buttonholes in the same position. Check the plackets lie flat and the gathers are even. Then close the cuff around a wrist. One or two fingers should fit inside.
For example, Grace in Benin City has a client with a 76 cm waist. Waistband ease is small, so she adds 1.5 cm, plus a 3 cm underlap for the hook. The finished band is 80.5 cm.

panel.heading: Grace cuts a skirt waistband
items: Mark and match centre back and sides
panel.rule: Waist + ease + underlap + two seam allowances.

say: With 1.5 cm seam allowances, she cuts 83.5 cm long. For a 3.5 cm band that folds in half, she cuts 10 cm wide.

panel.heading: Grace cuts a skirt waistband
items: Mark and match centre back and sides
panel.rule: Waist + ease + underlap + two seam allowances.

say: She checks the skirt waist measures 77.5 cm after the darts, so it fits without stretching. Then she matches the marked band to the skirt.

panel.heading: Grace cuts a skirt waistband
items: Mark and match centre back and sides
panel.rule: Waist + ease + underlap + two seam allowances.

say: For elastic, a common start is 85 to 90 percent of the waist, but always test it on the body. Make the casing only 0.5 to 1 cm wider than the elastic, overlap the ends 2 cm, and stitch in the ditch at the side seams so it cannot twist or roll.

panel.heading: Elastic waists and faced waists
left: Test the elastic on the body
Stitch in the ditch at sides
right: Tack to darts, seams, zip tape

say: A faced waist has no band. Interface the facing, trim, clip and understitch it, then tack it to the darts, seams and zip tape.

panel.heading: Elastic waists and faced waists
left: Test the elastic on the body
Stitch in the ditch at sides
right: Tack to darts, seams, zip tape

say: To remember. Trim the under collar slightly smaller. Staystitch and measure necklines before attaching. Calculate cuffs and waistbands from the body, plus ease, overlap and allowances. Check cuffs as a pair. And understitch every facing.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Trim the under collar 2 to 3 mm smaller
